title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The question mark in a glob
summary: Six settings accept glob patterns and none of them read the single character wildcard, which either matched the wrong files or stopped the scan outright.

highlights.title: One character, matched backwards
highlights.description: A pattern ending in Test?.kt kept Test.kt out of the report and let Test1.kt in, since the character stayed a regular expression quantifier and made the letter before it optional.

highlights.title: A pattern that stopped the whole scan
highlights.description: A question mark with nothing before it does not compile. In the command that runs every unused code check at once, one such pattern took all ten down.

highlights.title: One translator instead of three copies
highlights.description: Three providers each carried their own, so any glob fix had to be made three times. Compiled patterns are also kept now rather than rebuilt for every candidate: 34.5 ms against 5.1 ms over 40 000 calls.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A question mark in any ignore setting now covers exactly one character, and never crosses a path separator.
A pattern starting with a question mark no longer throws out of the detector.
The six settings that accept globs share one translator, and a test fails if a fourth copy of it appears.
Translated patterns are kept instead of being rebuilt on every candidate.
